transcript.text: Good question, Maya. Let me clarify. The assignment-consent package requirement applies specifically to the KITE and NORTHSTAR invoices — those are the ones whose contracts contain the anti-assignment provisions. If we want to include any KITE or NORTHSTAR receivables in the $7.2 million pool, we need signed consents from both customers before closing. If we exclude all KITE and NORTHSTAR invoices entirely, then no consent package is needed for them. However, I want to be precise: the $7.2 million figure I gave you already reflects the exclusion of the invoices under those two agreements. So as the pool currently stands — without consents — we're at $7.2 million and no consent package is required. If we later decide we want to recapture some of the excluded KITE or NORTHSTAR receivables to get closer to the original $8.5 million, then yes, we would need the signed assignment-consent package for both customers as a closing condition. I'd recommend we proceed on the $7.2 million basis unless there's a strong reason to pursue consents, given the June 30, 2026 closing timeline.
